newsitem.title: USA: AMP accepts estimates, sees goal delay.
newsitem.headline: AMP accepts estimates, sees goal delay.

text.p: AMP Inc agrees with analyst estimates the firm will earn $0.48 to $0.50 a share in the first quarter of 1997 and $2.16 for the year, investor relations director William Oakland said.

Oakland told an Emerald Asset Management investment forum the estimates do not include an expected $0.10-$0.15 per share first quarter one-time gain due to an accounting change, nor do they include possible negative currency effects from a stronger U.S. dollar.
Oakland also told the forum the company's financial targets for 2000 would probably be delayed due to an unexpectedly weak performance in 1996.

"We're seeing some negative currency effects," Oakland said in response to an investor's question. "We're for the time being agreeing with the $0.49," he said, referring to the average in the range of estimates he said earlier that the company was accepting.
However, he said, referring to some analysts' expectations of a quick rebound from 1996, "We're trying to keep expectations down."
"We think each quarter will get better," he said.
Oakland said the company retained its financial goals despite the expected delay.

"We are still confident we will reach these goals, but realize with 1996's performance well below trend line, it will probably take us a couple more years beyond 2000 to reach those ambitious targets," he said.
Those targets are annual sales of $10 billion, margins of 18 percent pre-tax and 10-12 percent after tax, and a return on equity of 18-20 percent.
"We are optimistic that we will be back on track this year with better sales growth and improved margins," he said.

"We think economic and market conditions are sufficiently favorable to permit better local currency growth this year in each region than in 1996. With the actions we are taking to eliminate some of our unprofitable products and consolidation of some facilities, operating margins should improve each quarter," Oakland said.
